run_summary.replication_search: A follow-up search for independent replication/reproduction of DTP, SRC, BI-R, and XdG did not surface a clear independent replication in this pass. This is absence-of-found-evidence, not evidence of absence.

candidates.mechanism: Dendritic target propagation (DTP): distal dendrites locally encode a mismatch between top-down excitation and learned lateral dendrite-targeting inhibition; this local dendritic state gates plasticity and nudges somatic activity, propagating target information through multilayer E/I circuits.
candidates.neuroscience_basis: Uses separate excitatory/inhibitory cell classes, segregated soma/distal dendrite compartments, dendrite-targeting interneurons, Dale-sign constraints, continuous bidirectional signaling, and experimentally motivated dendritic-spike-dependent plasticity including BTSP.
candidates.ai_transfer: Peer-reviewed Cell Reports 2026 computational study trains multilayer biology-constrained recurrent E/I ANNs on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and nonlinear spiral classification. DTP produced classification accuracy comparable to backpropagation when both trained the same biology-constrained architecture; BTSP-based updates also achieved MNIST performance comparable to the simpler dendritic-state rule. Fixed/random or independently learned top-down weights remained viable on MNIST, reducing dependence on exact weight symmetry.
quantitative_evidence: Five independent network instances were used for principal accuracy/error-alignment plots.

With fixed random top-down weights, the bottom-up/top-down alignment angle moved from 45 degrees initially to about 60 degrees by end of training while MNIST accuracy remained comparable to the symmetric-weight DTP condition.
BTSP uses eligibility/instructive interactions over a long temporal window up to approximately 5 seconds, and in DTP yielded MNIST performance comparable to LDS/backprop-like updates.
scope_limits: Supervised image/spiral tasks rather than autonomous long-horizon learning.
Exact numerical Fashion-MNIST/CIFAR-10 table values were not extracted in this run; source reports comparable accuracy to backpropagation on the same E/I architecture.
Independent external replication was not located in this pass.

primary_sources.title: Cellular and subcellular specialization enables biology-constrained deep learning

candidates.mechanism: Sleep Replay Consolidation (SRC): after ordinary task learning, drive spontaneous/noise-based network activity and apply local Hebbian-type plasticity offline to resurrect latent old-task structure and reduce cross-talk.
candidates.neuroscience_basis: Inspired by spontaneous replay during sleep and local plasticity; mechanistic toy analysis showed sleep updates down-scale task-irrelevant cross-talk pathways while residual old-task information remains in weights.
candidates.ai_transfer: Nature Communications 2022 study applied SRC to incremental MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CUB-200 and CIFAR-10, and combined it with rehearsal/iCaRL.
quantitative_evidence: CUB-200 sequential baseline after two tasks: task1 5%, task2 95%; with SRC: task1 63.2%, task2 45.4%.
CIFAR-10 overall incremental accuracy: 44% with SRC versus 19% without SRC.
Cross-modal MNIST/Fashion-MNIST: overall accuracy rose from 47% sequential baseline to 61% with SRC; joint-training reference was about 90%.
iCaRL on MNIST with K=100 exemplars: 65.5% versus 78.1% with iCaRL+SRC; K=200: 76.9% versus 84.5%.
At K=50, iCaRL+SRC after 1 epoch/task matched iCaRL after 10 epochs/task; averaged training savings were 3.73 epochs/task on MNIST, 3.67 on Fashion-MNIST, and 2.80 on CIFAR-10.
scope_limits: CIFAR-10 and CUB-200 experiments used pre-extracted/frozen visual features rather than end-to-end plastic convolutional stacks.
Sleep phase computational cost was reported as comparable to training an additional task in the studied batching setup.
Authors report OWM slightly surpassing SRC on most no-old-data class-incremental tasks; SRC's strongest case is complementarity with rehearsal and offline recoverability.
Independent external replication was not located in this pass.

primary_sources.title: Sleep-like unsupervised replay reduces catastrophic forgetting in artificial neural networks

candidates.mechanism: Brain-Inspired Replay (BI-R): replay internal/hidden representations generated through context-modulated feedback rather than reconstructing raw sensory inputs; combine conditional replay, context gating, replay-through-feedback and distillation.
candidates.neuroscience_basis: Motivated by hippocampal/cortical reactivation and the fact that internally generated representations need not recreate retinal-level inputs; early sensory processing is treated as relatively stable while higher representations are replayed.
candidates.ai_transfer: Nature Communications 2020 demonstrated no-data-storage continual learning on 100 permuted-MNIST tasks and split CIFAR-100, including class-incremental evaluation.
quantitative_evidence: On Class-IL split CIFAR-100, BI-R combined with Synaptic Intelligence achieved 0.344 +/- 0.002 average accuracy with replay-through-feedback versus 0.334 +/- 0.002 when that component was ablated.
On 100-task permuted MNIST, BI-R+SI achieved 0.904 +/- 0.005 versus 0.892 +/- 0.004 without replay-through-feedback.

Ablation experiments found internal replay to be the largest single contributor on CIFAR-100; for difficult settings the full combination outperformed any individual modification, with interactions larger than additive for some components.
scope_limits: CIFAR-100 experiments pre-trained convolutional layers on CIFAR-10 and froze them during continual learning; replay occurred through the later fully connected layers.
Class-IL performance remained substantially below joint-training upper bound.
Independent external replication was not located in this pass.

primary_sources.title: Brain-inspired replay for continual learning with artificial neural networks

candidates.mechanism: Context-dependent gating (XdG): activate sparse, mostly non-overlapping unit populations per task/context, reducing representational interference; combine with synaptic stabilization for complementary protection.
candidates.neuroscience_basis: Abstracts branch-/context-specific gating and sparse ensemble recruitment observed in cortical circuits/dendrites into task-conditioned unit gating.
candidates.ai_transfer: PNAS 2018 tested feedforward and recurrent networks under supervised and reinforcement learning across large task sequences.
quantitative_evidence: Evaluated on 100 sequential permuted-MNIST tasks and ImageNet split into 100 sequential tasks, plus 20 sequential cognitive tasks in RNNs.

XdG or synaptic stabilization alone only partially alleviated forgetting; their combination allowed high performance across the full task sequences with little forgetting, establishing complementarity rather than a single-mechanism effect.
scope_limits: Canonical XdG assumes task/context identity is available to select a gate; this is a major limitation for natural class-incremental settings with latent context.
Exact headline accuracies for the 100-task PNAS experiments were not extracted in this run.
Independent external replication was not located in this pass.

primary_sources.title: Alleviating catastrophic forgetting using context-dependent gating and synaptic stabilization

candidates.mechanism: Dendritic Localized Learning (DLL): pyramidal-neuron-inspired local forward/backward dynamics with trainable local feedback variables, intended to avoid weight symmetry, global error dependence and a distinct two-phase global training protocol.
candidates.neuroscience_basis: Inspired by dendritic dynamics/plasticity rather than a direct replication of a single biological experiment.
candidates.ai_transfer: ICML 2025 paper demonstrates learning across MLP, CNN and RNN architectures, with code released publicly.
quantitative_evidence: CNN average accuracy across MNIST/Fashion-MNIST/SVHN/CIFAR-10: DLL 86.61%, compared with Hebbian 57.43%, R-STDP 62.29%, Forward-Forward 10.67%, Equilibrium Propagation 18.50%, and backpropagation 90.67% under reported setups.
DLL CNN CIFAR-10 accuracy: 70.89% +/- 0.58%, versus backpropagation 75.10% +/- 0.54%.
DLL CNN SVHN accuracy: 85.81% +/- 0.17%, versus backpropagation 95.35% +/- 1.53%.
On Electricity time-series forecasting, DLL MSE/MAE 0.172/0.321 versus backpropagation 0.175/0.324, while character prediction lagged backpropagation (33.7% vs 51.9%).
scope_limits: Evidence is primarily algorithmic biological-plausibility benchmarking, not a continual-learning result and not a direct mapping from one experimentally isolated neural mechanism.
Sequential character prediction remained substantially below backpropagation.
No independent replication was located in this pass.
